Priya (support): Hey team, customer (tenant: acme-corp) reports repeated SSE disconnects and partial responses on streaming completions since yesterday. They see multiple reconnect loops and `write` failures in our logs. Asked for escalation :eyes:
Luca (cust): hitting this in prod, stream stops mid-output, client sees "connection reset" then reconnect; sometimes last chunk is truncated. Happening across multiple regions.
Maya (sre): can you paste the request-id for one of the affected streams? Also which SDK / client?
Luca (cust): request-id=rid-2026-03-11-7a12, using our node sdk (axios + EventSource polyfill) behind corporate SOCKS proxy.
Priya (support): thanks, grabbing logs and traces now. Initial service logs show repeated EAGAIN / EWOULDBLOCK on send, then the runtime aborts the connection after N retries:
```
[2026-03-11T14:12:03Z] pod=stream-serve-32 writev failed: errno=11 (Resource temporarily unavailable), attempts=3
[2026-03-11T14:12:03Z] pod=stream-serve-32 connection aborted: slow-consumer threshold exceeded, sent=172KB
```
Devon (engineer): that errno path is from our non-blocking socket code. We currently treat persistent EAGAIN + queued bytes > 256KB as an abort to protect memory.
Jon (eng-runtime): is the customer's client acking? For SSE we don't have per-chunk acks; slow consumer means kernel socket send buffer is full and proxy or client isn't reading. Any proxy logs?
Luca (cust): corp proxy shows chunked transfer buffering — it holds on to chunks until full then passes downstream. Also we saw long GC pauses in our app (node) which might be slowing reads.
Maya (sre): possible two factors: client-side read stalls + intermediary buffering (corporate proxy) causing prolonged sndbuf saturation on our side. Need to confirm sndbuf sizes and TCP stats. Can you run `ss -ti` on the stream pod and capture `sk_mem` counters?
Priya (support): asked customer for netstat and SDK trace. Meanwhile I pulled pod metrics: TX queue grows, retransmits spike, and write queue size on our side increases to ~300KB before abort.
Devon (engineer): short-term mitigation ideas: 1) lower server-side per-connection write batching (flush smaller chunks) 2) treat EAGAIN longer before abort (increase hysteresis) 3) advertise keepalive/ping and reduce outstanding KV cache pushes.
Jon (eng-runtime): lowering batch size is easiest to roll. We currently buffer ~128KB of model tokens before flush. Propose changing flush chunk to 8KB for streaming responses when `x-client-proxy` header detected. That will create more packets but reduces socket-saturation risk.
Priya (support): customer willing to test a server-side flag. They can route a subset of traffic to a canary.
Maya (sre): also ask customer to try direct connection (bypass corp proxy) to confirm proxy is contributing.
Luca (cust): we can test canary tomorrow morning. Also will try increasing socket buffer on client process as a quick test.
Jon (eng-runtime): one more note — our current abort classification lumps slow consumers with unroutable infra. We should add a distinct metric `stream.slow_consumer.abort_reason` with labels (sndbuf, proxy, client-pauses) for better debugging.
Devon (engineer): agreed, we'll add a trace span on send failure with `queued_bytes` and `sndbuf` snapshot.
Priya (support): escalation plan: 1) schedule canary with smaller chunk flush (Jon/Devon) 2) ask customer for direct-connect test and net stats (Maya) 3) add tracing/metric change (Devon) 4) if repro confirmed, ship runtime patch to avoid aggressive aborts (Jon). I've created an internal ticket and flagged eng-runtime + oncall.
alertbot: Deploy requested: canary/stream-flush-small -> staging, triggered by Jon at 2026-03-11T15:20:00Z
Jon (eng-runtime): deploying canary now, config: `STREAM_CHUNK_FLUSH_BYTES=8192` and `SLOW_CONSUMER_ABORT_THRESHOLD=512000` (temporary increase). Will monitor `stream.send.eagain` and `queued_bytes.gauge`.
Maya (sre): if we still see stuck connections, we'll capture `tcp_info` (`ss -ti`) and do a tcpdump to see retransmit patterns.
Luca (cust): thanks, we'll test tomorrow and share traces. Appreciate the quick triage.
Priya (support): follow-ups: gather request-ids for affected sessions, ask customer for their SDK version + Node GC traces, and collect proxy logs. Marking this P1 until canary results. :white_check_mark:
